title: Designing Hamiltonians with Exactly Flat Higher-Vortexable Bands
abstract: The zero modes of the Aharonov-Casher Hamiltonian form an exactly flat, vortexable Chern band in any nonuniform magnetic field, analogous to the lowest Landau level. We ask which local Hamiltonians host exactly flat higher-vortexable bands. For a scalar Hamiltonian, an exactly flat first-vortexable band requires a mass proportional to the local field; the Dirac analogue has the same structure. For periodic Bernal bilayer graphene with nonzero mean flux, the exact zero-mode pair is genuinely first-vortexable if and only if the interlayer hopping has nonzero mean; zero-mean hopping instead gives a decomposable pair. Multiorbital models yield exact higher-vortexable chains to arbitrary order, while remaining first order in momentum.
summary: This theoretical work investigates the conditions required for local Hamiltonians to support exactly flat, higher-vortexable bands, extending the concept from the lowest Landau level. By analyzing models like Bernal graphene, the authors establish a systematic method to construct these higher-order flat bands, showing that the mean magnetic flux is crucial for maintaining the topological integrity of the zero-mode complex.
main_problem: The paper aims to determine the necessary conditions for local Hamiltonians to host exactly flat, higher-vortexable Chern bands, analogous to the lowest Landau level.
main_result: Higher vortexability can be systematically constructed in multiorbital models, and the existence of these bands depends critically on the mean magnetic flux ($\langle B angle$) being non-zero to ensure the indecomposability of the vortexability chain.
method: The analysis involves deriving mathematical constraints on Hamiltonian coefficients by analyzing the closure conditions for higher-order zero modes and utilizing commutator identities.
model_or_system: The study examines scalar and Dirac Hamiltonians, and specifically applies the framework to Bernal-stacked bilayer graphene and general multiorbital systems characterized by a local magnetic field $B(r)$.
key_observables: Vortexability level ($n$), energy eigenvalues (especially zero modes), and the structure of the zero-mode complex.
important_parameters: Nonuniform magnetic field $B(r)$, mean magnetic flux $\langle B angle$, and the interlayer hopping parameter $\gamma$.
main_assumptions: The analysis often assumes the Hamiltonian can be written in a local single-particle form, and certain comparisons rely on specific ordering conventions (e.g., BenDaniel–Duke vs. von Roos).
figures_summary: Figures compare band structures, showing the difference between conventional AC Hamiltonians (only lowest band flat) and modified Hamiltonians that support multiple flat bands, and illustrate the structure of higher-vortexable multiorbital zero-mode complexes forming a Jordan chain.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first analyzing the simplest scalar and Dirac cases, then generalizing to the Bernal bilayer graphene model, and finally constructing a systematic, arbitrary-order hierarchy of vortexable bands using multiorbital operators and commutator algebra.
why_interesting: The concept of 'vortexability' provides a powerful topological invariant for characterizing flat bands, which is highly relevant for designing topological quantum materials and understanding edge/surface states in condensed matter systems.
